turns.t: Hello, doctor. Um, I've got this shake in my right hand, when I'm holding a cup of tea, and my daughter said I should see someone.
Tell me about the shake. When does it happen?
When I pick up the cup, and lift it, it trembles. And when I write, my handwriting gets scrawly. It's not there when the hand is resting.
When did you first notice it?
Oh, I'm not sure. A year ago? It could be longer. I forget these things.
Does it affect the other hand? ~
A little, I think, in the left, but not as much. ~
Does alcohol make it better or worse? ~
A glass of wine takes the edge off, actually. ~
Any slowness, stiffness, or trouble walking?
No, nothing like that. Walking's fine.
And caffeine, how much do you drink?
Four cups of tea a day.
Any allergies to medicines?
Years ago, I came out in a rash on penicillin, so I've stayed away.
Any other conditions?
High blood pressure, and an underactive thyroid.
Does tremor run in the family? ~
My father had it. We called it the family shake. ~
That's useful. Let me examine you. Hold your arms out. ~
Like this?
There's a fine tremor in both hands when you hold your arms out, worse on the right, and it increases when you reach for my finger. At rest it disappears.
Is it Parkinson's? ~
A rest tremor and slowness would be Parkinson's, and you don't have those. Let me check that. Walk across the room for me, and tap your fingers together. ~
Okay.
Your walking is normal, with good arm swing, and your finger-tapping is quick and even, with normal tone.
So it's not? ~
No, I'm not worried about Parkinson's. What you've got fits with a benign essential tremor, but I don't want to put a label on it yet. ~
What would you like me to do? ~
Try cutting down the tea to two cups. Caffeine makes tremors worse.
Two cups. I'll try. ~
And stress and tiredness too. It may settle. ~
Does it need tablets? ~
Not unless it's affecting your life. If it is, there are tablets that help. ~
It's the tea that bothers me. ~
Use a heavy cup, or a cup with two handles, and a straw if needed.
That's a good idea. ~
If the tremor becomes much worse, you develop stiffness or slowness, or it starts at rest, come back and I'll refer you to a neurologist.
I will. Thank you. ~
